items.title: The viewer's table of contents is a real macOS sidebar
items.text: The selected heading uses the system's own selection colors — an accent-filled pill while the window is focused, neutral gray when it isn't — and rows no longer shift as you scroll.

items.title: Resize the contents card
items.text: Drag its right edge and the card, the gutter, and the document's text column all move together. Your width is remembered across panes and sessions.

items.title: Clicking a heading takes you there and stays there
items.text: Your click pins the selection until your next scroll gesture, instead of the highlight walking off as the page smooth-scrolls.

items.title: A pinned "CONTENTS" header on Liquid Glass
items.text: Headings scroll underneath it, and long tables of contents now show a scroll indicator.

items.title: Glass cards line up
items.text: Every glass card leaves the same 12pt margin on all four sides, so their corners align and document text starts exactly one margin from the card.
